title: Estate Services Note: Expected Rotation of an Estate's Later Pass-Through Allocations (Capital Credits)
content:
# Expected Rotation of an Estate's Later Pass-Through Allocations

**Estate services note — Capital Credits (Patronage Capital).** The rotation an estate's pass-through row is expected on follows what the wholesale supplier has itself retired on the account:

- a pass-through year no later than the latest pass-through year the general retirements on the account have reached is already received and is expected in **zero** years (its rotation year is its own allocation year);
- a pass-through year at least **15** years later than that latest year, or on an account where no pass-through general retirement has ever been booked, is expected on the supplier's own rotation of **27** years (its rotation year is its allocation year plus 27);
- for any other pass-through year this rule sets no expected rotation.

## Reading the account

The **latest pass-through year reached** is the allocation year of the most recently booked general retirement entry on the deceased member's wholesale-supplier pass-through allocations.

## Decision table

| Account's pass-through general retirements | Pass-through year of the elected row | Expected in |
|---|---|---|
| latest year reached 1998 | 1998 or earlier | 0 years |
| latest year reached 1998 | 1999 to 2012 (1 to 14 years later) | not set by this rule |
| latest year reached 1998 | 2013 or later (15 or more years later) | 27 years |
| none ever booked | any | 27 years |

**Worked figure (hypothetical).** With the latest pass-through year reached at 1998, a 2024 pass-through row elected in 2026 is 26 years later than 1998, so it is expected on 27 years: rotation year 2051, 25 whole years after the year of the election.
